payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the source mug visibly positioned to the right of the same headphones, is there reliable evidence that no relevant progress occurred, or is the result unresolved?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Compare the source mug’s distinctive light-blue color, large body, and handle shape with edited mugs, allowing for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting. Fail only when evidence reliably establishes that no relevant progress toward moving the source mug occurred. Do not count a right-side mug alone as progress or fulfillment. A source-location blur or residue counts as evidence of attempted movement only if its shape and appearance reliably connect it to the source mug; an ambiguous color-like blur, unrelated or newly generated mugs, or uncertain identity does not establish progress. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish fulfillment or no progress.
node.binding: Compare the source image’s large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with each mug in the edited image; compare the same headphones across images and assess whether the source mug is to their right. Inspect the source mug’s former location for residue, but distinguish a visibly mug-shaped remnant corresponding to the source mug from an indistinct blur or artifact. Do not assume that a different-looking right-side mug is the source mug.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows two small gray/white mugs, neither clearly identifiable as the source’s large light-blue mug with its distinctive body and handle. A blue blur remains near the source mug’s former location, but it is indistinct and not reliably mug-shaped or identifiable as residue from that mug. The headphones are visible, but the source mug’s identity and movement cannot be established.

The high-confidence unknown merits review of the evidence-to-status criterion, not an automatic confidence reduction."}
